explanation: The Commission says the epsilon recalls the cradle of European civilization and the first letter of 'Europe', while the two parallel lines stand for stability.

claims.text: The European Commission states that the euro sign was inspired by the Greek letter epsilon.
The Commission does not cite sigma, eta or theta as the inspiration for the euro sign.
The Commission says the epsilon refers to the cradle of European civilization and to the first letter of the word 'Europe'.
According to the Commission, the two parallel lines of the euro sign represent the stability of the euro.
